# `move_focuser`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Move the electronic focuser to a target step.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds, by command-socket invocation, which always writes shared diagnostics); the effect of the handler itself is probable |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe7a10 (64-bit build), Move, GetValue |

Starts a focuser move and returns without waiting for motion to complete. On models with a wide-angle camera the request may be relayed to the peer processor before any local parsing; such a relayed reply is not described here. With ret_step true the reply result is an object with the clamped step instead of 0. The move happens before the optional return-step lookup, so an error from that lookup does not mean no motion occurred.

Side effects: Commands the focuser motor (eaf_move) and updates the stored focuser conversion state. Under some view-mode conditions on wide-camera models the request is relayed to the peer instead. No motion-complete wait.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"move_focuser"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | yes | - | [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (move_focuser success reply) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer\|object | yes | - | (move_focuser success reply) Integer 0 when ret_step is false; otherwise an object with the reported step. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (move_focuser success reply) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (move_focuser success reply) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | step missing, null or not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 318 | Focuser handle is not open (before the move, or in the post-move lookup) | `device not connected` |
| 300 | Conversion numerator or denominator is not positive, or the driver move call fails | `internal error` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Errors produced on the peer when the request is relayed are unresolved.

## Example

Request, move - Move to a target and ask for the step back:

```json
{"id":41,"method":"move_focuser","params":{"step":1200,"ret_step":true}}
```

Reply, ok-with-step:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"move_focuser","result":{"step":1200},"code":0,"id":41}
```

Reply, ok-plain:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"move_focuser","result":0,"code":0,"id":42}
```

Reply, missing-step:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"move_focuser","error":"expected int param","code":104,"id":43}
```
